author: reek
body: `-gop-stride` is the machine option that makes them differ, so this test's subject is the MACHINE and its `.vmargs` sidecar is the test. The geometry is read from the cells codex-vm publishes rather than written here: reading them is what proves the option reached the guest at all, and a hardcoded 512 would pass just as well with the bed switched off.

author: reek
body: Painting w columns per row into a stride-wide buffer with the wrong multiplier writes one contiguous run of w*h pixels: the run spills into the invisible pad of the early rows, and it runs out before the bottom row is reached. A test that checked only that something got painted would pass with either renderer.

author: reek
body: The three assertions cover two independent paths, which the sabotage is what established -- the first attempt set `r3t-stride` to the width and only two rows moved, because `r3d-target-at` hands `r3d-fill-rows` the stride argument directly and never reads the field back. So the pad and the plot answer for `r3d-plot`, the bottom row answers for `r3d-fill-rows`, and they are not one defect seen from two ends.

author: reek
body: Measured against seed 6671C19A0F78F630 with both arms sabotaged to step by the width: the pad, the bottom row and the plot all go from `yes` to `no`, and `stride exceeds width` stays `yes`.

author: reek
body: `stride exceeds width` is the control. It is a property of the bed and not of the renderer, so it holds under sabotage; if it ever reads `no` the machine option is off and the other three rows are answering a question nobody asked. Running without the sidecar is what shows that, and it reads `no` exactly as it should.

author: reek
body: Counts surviving sentinel pixels in the invisible pad of one row, then across every row. Indexing here is by stride deliberately: this walks the buffer as the hardware scans it, which is the frame of reference the question is asked in.
